me.get.summary: See who you are, your names and workspaces
me.get.description: Call this first. Returns your main name and personas (pass one as `as` to write or comment under it), every workspace you are on with your role there (pass its address as `workspace` to other tools), and short guidance. Readers cannot tell your personas are you; never mention which names belong together in posts or comments. Pass `workspace` to also get what you can do there.

identities.list.summary: Your names: your main name and personas
identities.list.description: Lists the names you write and comment under, with each one's address and post count. Only you see that they belong together.

workspaces.create.summary: Start a new workspace for a team
workspaces.create.description: Creates a workspace at /<slug> with you as its owner, and returns it. Ask the person for the name first; the address defaults to the name. logo: optional, a square image's /media address from media_upload or media_list.

posts.list.summary: List posts you can edit: drafts and published
posts.list.description: Writers see posts on their own blog and personas they were given; admins see every post. Filter by status (draft, published, all), by blog with `as`, and with `page` true for the workspace's pages only or false for posts only. Each post has an id for posts.get and posts.update, its public url, whether it is a page, and counts of claps, comments and pending comments.

posts.get.summary: Read one post with its full Markdown
posts.get.description: Pass the post's id, or its address (url) such as /@team/launch-notes. Published posts are readable by anyone signed in; drafts only by people who can edit them. Returns title, subtitle, tags, cover, status, whether it is a page, and the Markdown body.

posts.create.summary: Write a new post (draft by default) in Markdown
posts.create.description: Writers only. Body is Markdown (GitHub style): headings, lists, tables, code, links, images. Extras: a line `> [!NOTE]` (or TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION) starts a callout; a YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, CodePen, Figma or Spotify link alone on a line becomes an embed; a link to another post on Margin alone on a line becomes a card; `![alt](/media/<id>.<ext> "caption")` on its own line is a figure (add photos, drawings and videos with media_upload or media_link; pages pick the right size themselves), add #wide or #full to the address for width; .mp4 or uploaded videos play inline. Code: fence it with its language (```js, ```python, ```sql…) and it is highlighted. Maths: LaTeX between $…$ inline, or $$ on lines of their own around a display formula (a dollar amount like $5 stays text; write \$ for a literal one). Leave the H1 out: the title is shown above the body. The address is made from the title unless you pass slug. Use `as` to post under one of your names, or as the workspace itself (its address) if you own or run it. `cover` takes a photo's /media address, or `drawing` gives the post a drawn cover in the workspace's style (pick its subject); with neither, the post has no cover. For a picture in the workspace's style, use covers_prompt first; pass its tone as cover_tone with the cover. Status draft keeps it private; published puts it live at once. Unless the person asked to publish, create a draft and give them the preview link. Drawn covers: week (calendars, time), energy (power, hardware), people (research), network (sync, devices), stack (layers, documents, process), inbox (messages, support), bars (numbers, speed), rings (sound, quiet, focus). Pass `workspace` (its address, from me_get). `featured` pins it on the workspace home (owners and admins). `page: true` makes a page instead (owners and admins): written as the workspace, at its address plus the slug (/about may be one), with no date, byline, claps or comments, and left out of the home, Latest, topics and the feed; link it from the menu with workspace_update's nav.

posts.update.summary: Edit, publish or unpublish a post
posts.update.description: Pass the post id and only the fields to change; the rest stay. markdown replaces the whole body, so read the post first with posts.get and send back the edited text. status published puts it live (drafts) and draft takes it down. A draft's address follows its title until first published; after that it changes only when you pass slug, and the old address redirects. `as` moves the post to another blog you can write as. `cover` sets a photo (cover_alt describes it; cover_tone is the tone covers_prompt gave, so the next cover differs). `drawing` changes the drawn cover (week, energy, people, network, stack, inbox, bars, rings, or none to remove the cover). `page` true turns a post the workspace wrote as itself into a page, false turns a page back into a post; the address stays. `published_at` (Margin's admins) sets the date the post shows; on a draft never published it waits until the post goes live, and the draft's address still follows its title.

posts.delete.summary: Delete a post with its comments and claps
posts.delete.description: Permanent. Only for someone who can edit the post. Confirm with the person before calling; to take a post down without losing it, use posts.update with status draft.

comments.inbox.description: Comments on your posts waiting for approval, or not yet answered. Writers and admins. pending: comments held for approval. unanswered: threads whose latest message is not from the post's blog. Each item has the comment, the quoted passage it is about (if any), the comment it replies to, and the post. To help the writer: reply with comments.reply only to ordinary comments that a friendly, short answer settles (thanks, simple questions the post answers, clarifications). Do not reply, and ask the writer instead, when a comment is a complaint, criticism that needs judgment, legal, medical, financial or security matters, personal data, pricing or promises, anything heated or political, or anything you are unsure about. Approve or reject pending comments only when the writer asked you to. Covers one workspace; pass `workspace`.

comments.list.summary: Read every comment on a post, with quotes and replies
comments.list.description: Pass post_id. Returns the comments you may see, oldest first: each has its quoted passage (for notes on a highlight), its parent_id when it is a reply, its author and its status.

comments.reply.description: Answers as the post’s blog by default. Plain text, a few sentences, in the writer's voice; links are fine. Writers who edit the post answer as its blog unless `as` names another. Only reply to ordinary comments a short answer settles; for anything sensitive, critical, legal, personal, about money or promises, or that you are unsure of, ask the writer first and do not reply.

comments.create.description: Optionally on a quoted passage, or as one of your personas. post_id and body are required. quote.exact anchors the comment to a passage of the post (copy it exactly, 600 characters at most; prefix and suffix are the few words around it when the passage repeats). parent_id makes it a reply. Writers may comment under one of your names with `as`. sample true marks a comment as sample content, shown only to the team: use it to fill a post with example discussion for screenshots or design reviews. Never post invented comments as if they were real readers on a live blog.

comments.moderate.summary: Approve, reject or delete a comment
comments.moderate.description: For the post's writers and admins (anyone may delete their own comment). approve shows a held comment; reject hides it; delete removes it and its replies. Only act when the writer asked you to.

personas.create.summary: Create a persona: a shared identity people can post and comment as
personas.create.description: Adds a persona: another name you can write and comment under, with its own handle, bio and picture. Readers can't tell it is you.

personas.update.summary: Change one of your names (name, bio, picture)
personas.update.description: Updates your main name or a persona of yours. Workspace owners can also rename the workspace's own voice by its address. An empty avatar removes the picture.

personas.delete.description: Removes a persona of yours that has no posts (delete or move its posts first). Comments written under it stay, shown as @handle. Confirm with the person before calling.

media.list.summary: List your photos, drawings and videos to use in posts
media.list.description: Your uploads (admins see everyone's), newest first. Each has its /media address, the Markdown to put on a line of its own in a post, its pixel size, and sizes: smaller copies (w640 … w2048, and og, the 1200 × 630 crop link previews use) that Margin makes on first request. Pages pick the right copy themselves; use a size's address only where you need a small file. Add files with media_upload or media_link.

media.upload.summary: Add a drawing (SVG) or a small photo to your library
media.upload.description: Returns the file's address and the Markdown to put on a line of its own in a post (![alt](/media/…)). svg: a drawing as SVG text with a viewBox, plain shapes and text and inline styles; scripts, embedded images and links to other files are refused (512 KB at most). data: a small photo (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF) in base64, up to about 1.5 MB; for anything bigger, a photo the person has, or a video, use media_link. Always give alt: what the image shows. Photos larger than 2048 px are shrunk.

media.link.summary: Get a link that adds photos and videos to your library
media.link.description: For an hour, the link takes up to 10 files into the person's library: photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF; 12 MB each), SVG drawings and videos (MP4, WebM or MOV; 20 MB each). Give it to the person to open on their phone or computer; the page shrinks photos before sending. With a shell, send files yourself, one per request: curl -sS -F file=@photo.jpg -F alt="what it shows" <url>. Each answer has the address and Markdown; media_list shows them too. Margin shrinks photos larger than 2048 px but can't turn them, so send photos upright, and video as H.264 MP4 so every browser plays it.

workspace.get.summary: See a workspace's settings (owners and admins)
workspace.get.description: Returns the workspace's name, tagline, description, home, moderation, cover style, cover recipe (cover_recipe, with custom listing the parts changed from the default), theme, menu links, pinned posts, footer line, whether Margin's credit shows, and its byline photo (avatar: an address, or "" when the logo stands in; avatar_source: photo, profile or logo), with your role. Change them with workspace.update, the theme with themes.activate, and the team with team.list and team.update.

workspace.update.summary: Change a workspace's settings (owners and admins)
workspace.update.description: Updates the workspace: name, tagline, description, home ("latest", "curated" for pinned posts first, or "@handle" to make one writer's page the home), moderation ("off", "outsiders": hold comments from names not on the team, "all"), cover style (look paper|flat|blocks, tone lilac|tangerine|mint|butter|sky|coral) and menu links. cover_recipe: how assistants make cover pictures in the workspace's style (covers_prompt hands it to writers); send only the parts to change, null resets a part, and cover_recipe: null resets it all. style is the prompt's fixed text, with {tone} and {accent} where the colours go; tones are the backgrounds covers take in turn (1 to 8, each { name, hex }); accent is one { name, hex } used sparingly; subjects says how to pick a post's subject; references are up to 4 /media addresses of covers in the style; alt says how to describe one. Until changed, it follows the drawn-cover style. logo: a square image's /media address (from media_upload, media_list or an upload link); an empty string removes it. It becomes the tab icon; a PNG or JPEG of 512 px or more is also the home-screen icon, the app icon and the picture in link previews of pages without a cover, which an SVG can't be. avatar: the byline photo, the picture beside the workspace's own name on its posts, cards and comments, apart from the logo, which stays the site's mark: a /media address, "me" for your own Holm profile photo (it follows your profile), or "" to show the logo there again. footer: one line for the footer, plain text where [label](https://…) makes a link and {year} prints the year; an empty string brings back the theme's own. credit: false hides "Written on Margin", the Holm mark and Send feedback from the footer.

workspace.leave.description: Takes you off the workspace. Your posts there stay up under your names. The last owner can't leave; make someone else an owner first with team.update. Confirm with the person before calling.

team.list.summary: List a workspace's team and open invites (owners and admins)
team.list.description: Returns each member (account id, role, name, picture, email, the names they write under, when they joined; you is true for the caller) and every invite not revoked (id, email, role, who sent it, expiry, used). Pass an account to team.update and an invite id to invites.revoke.

team.update.summary: Change someone's role, or remove them (owners and admins)
team.update.description: role is owner, admin, writer, or remove to take them off the workspace (their posts stay). Only owners add or remove owners, and a workspace keeps at least one owner. Confirm removals with the person first.

themes.list.summary: List the themes a workspace can use, and which is live
themes.list.description: Owners and admins. Built-in themes (quiet, editorial), Margin's library, and this workspace's own (scope "workspace", id "<workspace>/<id>"; up to 3, which only this workspace sees), with the live one (active; active_rev is the save of an own theme the site shows) and each theme's comment layout.

themes.reference.summary: How themes work: files, template data, hooks and rules
themes.reference.description: Read this before changing a theme. It lists every file a theme has, the data each page template receives, the hooks a theme must print, how settings and queries work, and what the validator refuses.

themes.get.summary: Download every file of a theme to study or change
themes.get.description: Files as path → text (theme.json, templates, partials, CSS), and binaries (fonts, images) with their /t/… addresses. Built-in and library themes: anyone signed in. A workspace's own (id "<workspace>/<id>", add @<rev> for an earlier save): its owners and admins; revisions lists its last saves and live_rev the one the site shows. To restyle a workspace: get a theme, change only what you need, save with themes.save (base plus the changed files), open the preview link, then themes.activate. A copy of a built-in keeps the built-in's fonts at /t/<id>.b1/…; leave those addresses as they are.

themes.validate.summary: Check a theme without saving it
themes.validate.description: Checks a theme without saving it. files: path → text, fonts and images as { base64 }. With workspace and base, checks base with your files laid over it, exactly as themes.save would store it. Returns ok, errors (each with file, line and message) and warnings. Fix every error before themes.save.

themes.save.summary: Save a theme of the workspace's own, to preview before it goes live
themes.save.description: Owners and admins. Saves one of the workspace's own themes (up to 3; only this workspace sees them), as a new save. Start from base (a theme you can read: "quiet", a library id, or "<workspace>/<id>", with @<rev> for an earlier save) and send only the files you change: text as strings, fonts and images as { base64 }, { from: "<a /t/… address from themes.get>" } to keep one, or null to remove a file. Keep each call under about 45 KB. Without base, saving under the id of one of your themes starts from its latest save. theme.json's id names the theme; a copy of a built-in needs a new id. A theme with errors is not saved: the answer lists them. Saving never changes the live site, even for the live theme: open preview_url, then themes.activate. To go back, activate <id>@<rev> from themes.get.

themes.activate.summary: Make a theme live, and optionally change its settings
themes.activate.description: Owners and admins. Makes a theme live on the workspace, and optionally sets its settings (as declared in its theme.json, such as accent colour or landing text; omitted ones keep their values). id is from themes.list. One of the workspace's own goes live at its latest save, or at an earlier one with <id>@<rev> (going back).

themes.delete.summary: Delete one of the workspace's own themes
themes.delete.description: Owners and admins. Removes one of the workspace's own themes and all its saves for good; not the live one. Without confirm it answers with what would go: ask the person, then call again with confirm: true.

themes.publish.summary: Add a workspace's theme to Margin's library
themes.publish.description: Margin's admins. Copies one of a workspace's own themes (its latest save, or <id>@<rev>) into Margin's library, under its own id or library_id, so every workspace can pick it. Replaces a library theme with that id; workspaces using it see the new one.

covers.prompt.summary: Get the workspace's cover recipe to make a cover in its style
covers.prompt.description: Writers. Margin makes no pictures: this hands you the workspace's cover recipe so your own image tool can make a cover in its style. Pass post_id (the post it's for) and, once you've chosen it, subject: one or two sentences on the one object or scene that stands for this post's idea (follow subjects). Returns tone (this cover's background, chosen so covers side by side differ; pass its name back as cover_tone), accent, style and framing (the fixed parts), prompt (all of it, when subject is given), references (covers in this style to match), image (size, and the safe area pages crop to), alt (how to describe it) and steps. Show the person the picture before you attach it, unless they said not to.

invites.create.summary: Invite someone to write on this blog
invites.create.description: Creates a single-use invite link to write in the workspace (owners and admins). With an email, only that address can use it, and Margin emails it when the node can send mail.

invites.revoke.summary: Cancel an invite link (owners and admins)
invites.revoke.description: Pass the invite's id (from invites.create or team.list). The link stops working; anyone who already joined stays.
